Convert a caugi to a data.frame

Source: R/methods.R
as.data.frame.caugi.Rd

Returns the graph as a plain data.frame with columns from, edge and to: one row per edge, then one row per isolated node with the node in from and NA in edge and to. caugi() reads such rows back as isolated nodes, so caugi(edges_df = as.data.frame(cg)) keeps every node. Use edges() for the edges alone. The graph class is kept in the "graph_class" attribute, which as_caugi() uses as its default class, so as_caugi(as.data.frame(cg)) gives back cg.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'caugi'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A caugi object.

row.names, optional

Passed to base::as.data.frame().

...

Passed to base::as.data.frame().

Value

A data.frame with columns from, edge and to, and a "graph_class" attribute.

See also

Other caugi methods: caugi-equality, length.caugi(), print.caugi(), summary.caugi()

Examples

cg <- caugi(A %-->% B + C, B %---% C, D, class = "PDAG")
df <- as.data.frame(cg) # D has a row with edge = NA
caugi(edges_df = df, class = "PDAG") == cg # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
